changes.new: 2.4 EULA Acceptance Gate — Mandatory Before a Listing Goes Live

changes.old: You must read and accept this EULA before your registration is created on the Platform. The acceptance process is as follows:
changes.new: You must read and accept this EULA before any listing of yours goes live on the Platform. A listing may be saved as a draft before you accept, but a draft is never shown to Buyers. The acceptance process is as follows:
changes.why: Drafts exist before acceptance, so 'before your registration is created' is contradicted by the app; the server refuses to publish until acceptance is recorded (EULA-PUBLISH-1).

changes.old:
1. You receive a Magic Link via email or click a sign-up link on the Platform.

  2. On clicking the link, an EULA acceptance screen is presented as the first step before any registration or listing data is created.

  3. You must tick "I have read and agree to the Terms of Use / EULA and Privacy Policy" and click "Accept and Continue".

  4. The Platform records your acceptance timestamp and EULA version number. This record is stored in the Platform's database and constitutes your binding agreement.

  5. Clicking "Accept and Continue" constitutes your electronic signature on this Agreement per Section 4 of the ECT Act.
changes.new:
1. You start a listing from a Magic Link sent to you, from the sell flow in the Platform's app, or from the Platform's Quick page.

  2. In the sell flow, the acceptance is set out directly above the publish button, with this EULA linked: "By tapping Publish now you confirm: I have read and accept the TrustSquare Seller Terms, and confirm all listing information is accurate. I understand that listings with inappropriate content will be permanently removed." Tapping "Publish now — I accept the Terms" is your acceptance.

  3. When you publish a saved draft — for example from a Magic Link or from your Seller Hub — the step headed "Almost live" shows this EULA in full. Once you have scrolled to the end, you must tick "I have read and accept the TrustSquare Seller Terms, and confirm all listing information is accurate" and "I understand that listings with inappropriate content will be permanently removed", and tap "Go live".

  4. If you save an edit to a listing, or publish from elsewhere in the app, before you have accepted this EULA, this EULA is shown in full on a Terms sheet: you must scroll to the end, tick the same two confirmations and tap "I accept".

  5. Unless you have already accepted this EULA, a listing saved on the Quick page is kept as a draft and goes live only after you have read and accepted this EULA in the Platform's app.

  6. If this EULA changes materially after you have accepted it, you are asked to accept it again, in the same way, the next time you publish or edit a listing.

  7. The Platform records your acceptance timestamp and EULA version number. This record is stored in the Platform's database and constitutes your binding agreement.

  8. Tapping "Publish now — I accept the Terms", "Go live" or "I accept" constitutes your electronic signature on this Agreement per Section 4 of the ECT Act.
changes.why: Replaces the 'Accept and Continue' flow, which exists nowhere in the app, with the acceptance points it actually uses (ms.js sell-flow scorecard and _tsSellerTermsGate, marketsquare.html 'Almost live' step sob-p3, bea_main.py quick_publish and EULA-VERSION-1), keeping the timestamp-and-version record (users.eula_accepted_at plus the eula_version trigger).

needs_david.section: 5.3 (Casuals and Adventures rows, 'Adventures — No Trust Score Penalty' box) and 4.9
needs_david.question: Should Casuals and Adventures Sellers be exempt from the −5 for ignoring an Introduction? The Terms promise them no penalty, but the code gives every category except Local Market the same −5 (bea_main.py _lifecycle_sweep), and the app's own 'How introductions work' table shows −5 for Accommodation and Experiences. Options: (a) Drop the exemption from 5.3 (the Casuals and Adventures rows and the 'Adventures — No Trust Score Penalty' box), so the Terms match the code and the app. (b) Build the exemption into the code (skip the −5 for Casuals and Adventures in _lifecycle_sweep) and correct the app's table. Recommended: (a), because your RESP-1 ruling of 23 Jul 2026 (docs/TRUST_SCORE_CRITERIA.md, Amendment v1.3) applies the −5 to every standard Introduction and the app already tells Adventures Sellers so. The text is left as it stands in this draft.

Which legal basis should the new banking row give? Options: (a) Consent, given when the Seller adds the details (as drafted, like the certification-documents row). (b) Contractual necessity. (c) Legitimate interest. Recommended: (a), because adding banking details is optional in the app (a 2-point trust signal, POST /users/{email}/banking) and nothing in the contract depends on them.

Should the banking row keep 'Tuppence purchases' as a purpose? It is your wording and the in-app form says the details are used 'when you buy Tuppence', but no purchase code reads the stored banking details — Paystack takes the payment details itself. Options: (a) Keep the purpose as worded. (b) Drop it from this row and from the in-app form text, leaving confirmation of identity as the purpose. Recommended: (b), because POPIA requires the stated purpose to be the real one, and today the details are used only for the name match against the verified ID and as a trust signal.

Should v1.19 be marked a material change? bea_main.py has EULA_CURRENT_VERSION = '1.18' and EULA_MATERIAL_VERSION = '1.16'. Options: (a) Material: set EULA_MATERIAL_VERSION to '1.19', so every Seller accepts again at their next publish or edit, after the 14 days' notice that Section 15.1 requires. (b) Not material: bump only EULA_CURRENT_VERSION to '1.19'. Recommended: (a), because v1.19 rewrites what Sellers agreed to on identity checks (3.4–3.5), how Tuppence moves (5.1, 6.3) and AI prices (5.5), and re-acceptance is what binds existing Sellers to the corrected text. Nothing outside the two draft files was touched.

What should the Sellers' liability cap in 10.6 be? It is 'the total Tuppence earned and credited to your Wallet' in the 12-month period, but a Seller is never credited Tuppence for an Introduction (bea_main.py accept_intro burns the Buyer's hold; only Local Market no-show credits exist), so the cap is in practice about zero. Options: (a) The same as Buyers: ZAR 500. (b) The Tuppence the Seller bought or spent on the Platform in that period, valued at USD $2 each. (c) The greater of (a) and (b). Recommended: (c), because a cap of about zero risks being struck out as unfair under the CPA, while (c) keeps a floor and tracks what the Seller actually paid. The text is left as it stands; 5.1, 6.3 and 12.3 were corrected.

Should a Property listing really pause and take one Buyer at a time? The Terms, canon A3 (PRINCIPLE_REQUIREMENTS.md) and docs/LISTING_STATE_MACHINE.md say so, but the server never pauses the listing or limits requests (bea_main.py create_intro): only the requesting Buyer's own screen shows it paused, and the app's 'How introductions work' table says 'Up to 3' and groups Cars with Property. Options: (a) Build it: the server pauses a Property listing on a request and refuses others until it is answered, and the 'Up to 3' copy is corrected. (b) Retire the Commitment model: Property runs Soft Queue, and the Terms, canon A3 and the app copy say so. (c) Cap it at 3 open requests per Property listing, enforced by the server, with the Terms and canon changed to match. Recommended: (a), because canon A3 may not change without full council review and the Terms, listing screen and state machine already describe it, so only the server is out of line. The Property row is left as it stands; this draft adds Cars as Soft Queue, as the sell flow runs it (marketsquare.html CATS.Cars), so if you choose (a) or (c), say whether Cars follows Property.

How should the Terms cover Local Market? It is live but runs under its own six in-app clauses (marketsquare.html, 'Local Market — Terms') with a Seller-pays model: the Seller pays 1T (2T if boosted) when the first request on a listing arrives, Buyers pay nothing, and there are no-show credits and a suspension ladder (bea_main.py /local-market/intro; docs/LOCAL_MARKET_REQUIREMENTS.md). The EULA never mentions it, and the model conflicts with 2.6 and 5.1 ('the party seeking the service always pays') and with canon A8's list of allowed deductions. Options: (a) Fold Local Market into the EULA: name it in 2.1 and 4.4, add 5.3 and 7.1 rows, and state the Seller-pays exception in 2.6 and 5.1. (b) Keep it separate: name it in 2.2 as governed by supplemental Local Market Terms, and publish those clauses alongside the EULA. Recommended: (a), because a Seller who pays should find the fee in the Terms they accept, and the six clauses are short enough to fold in. Cars was added in this draft; Local Market was not.

Should the Adventures bonus table match what the app actually awards? The live catalogue (bea_main.py _CATEGORY_SIGNALS; docs/TRUST_SCORE_CRITERIA.md) gives TGCSA 1–5 star 6/10/14/18/22 (table: 5/10/15/20/25), first aid 6 (table: 5) and CATHSSETA 8 (table: 10), and has no SATSA, FEDHASA, liquor-licence or PDP/SABOA credential at all. Options: (a) Replace the table with the catalogue's Adventures credentials and points. (b) Change the app to the table: add the four missing credentials to the catalogue and use the table's values. (c) Drop the table and rely on the 'Bonus Values Are Indicative' box, which already says the in-app criteria govern. Recommended: (a), because the Terms should not promise bonuses the app never awards, and the catalogue is the canon the app shows each Seller.

What should 11.4 say? It suspends an account whose Trust Score 'falls below 0', which cannot happen because the score is held between 0 and 100 (bea_main.py _trust_math), and no code suspends an account for a low score except in Local Market, which suspends a Local Market Seller below 30 with an active complaint (_lm_apply_suspension). Options: (a) Delete 11.4, because 10.2 and the blocking causes in 14.5 already cover suspension. (b) Keep a low-score suspension but make it real: pick a reachable threshold and build it. (c) Replace it with the Local Market rule once Local Market is in the Terms. Recommended: (a), because a clause that can never trigger protects nobody, and 14.5 already lists every cause for blocking an account.

Should Buyers formally accept the Terms somewhere? Only Sellers do today (before a listing goes live, plus the separate Buzz and Local Market acceptances: bea_main.py /users/{email}/eula, /buzz/accept, /local-market/eula/accept), so 'By accepting this EULA' in 2.5 (age and capacity warranties) and 9.3 (POPIA consent) never binds a Buyer. Options: (a) Add a one-tap Buyer acceptance, recorded with timestamp and version like the Seller's, at the first Introduction request or first Tuppence top-up. (b) Reword 2.5 and 9.3 to 'By using the Platform', relying on use alone. Recommended: (a), because POPIA consent and an ECT Act signature both need a positive act, and the first request or top-up is where a Buyer first commits money.

Do the countries the Quick page is set up for need a Country Schedule? Quick packs exist for ZA, NA, BW, MZ, KE, GB, DE, AU and US (roles/quick_country_packs.json), so Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique, Kenya and Germany get a localised Quick page but no Schedule, while France, Portugal, New Zealand and Argentina have a Schedule but no Quick pack.
